name: Georgetown University
character: The compact 104-acre hilltop campus overlooks the Potomac River, featuring Neo-Medieval Healy Hall, traditional quadrangles, fountains, flowers, and groves of trees.

landmarks.name: Healy Hall
landmarks.quote: Healy Hall, designed by Paul J. Pelz in Neo-Medieval style and built from 1877 to 1879

landmarks.name: Healy Gates
landmarks.quote: The main gates, known as the Healy Gates, are located at the intersection of 37th and O Streets NW

landmarks.name: Dahlgren Quadrangle
landmarks.quote: the main campus has traditionally centered on Dahlgren Quadrangle behind Healy Hall
landmarks.look: Traditional open quadrangle behind Healy Hall.

landmarks.name: Red Square
landmarks.quote: Red Square has replaced the Dahlgren Quadrangle as a center of student life.

landmarks.name: Riggs Library
landmarks.quote: Within Healy Hall are a number of notable rooms including Gaston Hall, Riggs Library, and the Bioethics Library Hirst Reading Room.

landmarks.name: Gaston Hall
landmarks.quote: Within Healy Hall are a number of notable rooms including Gaston Hall, Riggs Library, and the Bioethics Library Hirst Reading Room.
landmarks.look: Notable hall room inside Healy Hall.

landmarks.name: Georgetown University Astronomical Observatory
landmarks.quote: Both Healy Hall and the Georgetown University Astronomical Observatory, built in 1844, are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

landmarks.name: Regents Hall
landmarks.quote: Regents Hall, the new science building, opened in Fall 2012.
landmarks.look: Large science hall overlooking a scenic lawn.
